worksheet.intro: The capstone of the function-field-generation segment, presented mathematics-first. Every definition and statement here is Lean, and is exhibited by `#check` or `#print`; every proof body is a semi-formal argument: what is to be proved, what each hypothesis supplies, and which proven theorem or earlier step meets each premise. Narratives live in comments. The source of this sheet is presentation/function-field-generation/capstone.json.

conventions.math: The field of Laurent series over ℚ. It is the single ambient field in which every function of the theorem lives; there is no upper half-plane and no analytic continuation anywhere.
The classical j-invariant, as the explicit Laurent series q⁻¹ + 744 + 196884 q + ⋯ ∈ ℚ((q)).
The nome substitution q ↦ q^N applied to j(q): every exponent is multiplied by N. In Lean this is qExpand ℚ N jq, abbreviated jqN N.
The two-generator field ℚ(j(q), j(q^N)) ⊂ ℚ((q)).
The full divisor field ℚ(j(q^d) : d ∣ N) ⊂ ℚ((q)). This is the field the formalization takes as the function field of X₀(N).
The Dedekind psi function Σ_{d ∣ N, d squarefree} N/d = N ∏_{p ∣ N}(1 + 1/p): the index [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ₀(N)], hence the degree of the cover X₀(N) → X(1) and the Y-degree of the modular equation Φ_N.
The modular polynomial: Φ_N ∈ ℤ[j][Y], monic in Y, of Y-degree ψ(N), vanishing at (X, Y) = (j(q), j(q^N)). Lean packages it with its three facts as ModularPolynomialData N.
The relative degree of a field extension K ⊆ L, with K the base field. In Lean: IntermediateField.relfinrank K L, or Module.finrank K L for a simple extension.
x is integral over ℤ[j(q)] when there is a monic P ∈ ℤ[j(q)][Y] with P(x) = 0. This is exactly the existence of a monic annihilator, which is what Lean's IsIntegral unpacks to.
Tight d: [ℚ(j)(j(q^d)) : ℚ(j)] = ψ(d). Gen d: F_d = F_d^full. Hall N: for every d ∣ N, both Tight d and Gen d.

The composed substitution q ↦ u q^e, for a unit u in a coefficient field K: qExpand K e (qTwist u (coeffEmb K j(q))). It is the nome form of the affine map τ ↦ eτ + (const) and is named TS K e u in the port.

definitions.name: ModularCurve.qExpand
definitions.lean:
def qExpand (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] :
    LaurentSeries R →+* LaurentSeries R
definitions.math: The substitution q ↦ q^N on Laurent series: a monomial q^k becomes q^{Nk}, coefficients unchanged. It is a ring endomorphism, and it is injective because N ≠ 0.
definitions.heading: `qExpand` — the q ↦ q^N substitution

definitions.name: ModularCurve.qTwist
definitions.lean: def qTwist {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (u : Rˣ) : LaurentSeries R →+* LaurentSeries R
definitions.math: The rescaling q ↦ u q for a unit u: the coefficient of q^k is multiplied by u^k. Composed with qExpand e it is the substitution q ↦ u q^e, which the port writes TS K e u; this is the nome form of τ ↦ eτ + (const).
definitions.heading: `qTwist` — the q ↦ u q rescaling

definitions.name: ModularCurve.coeffEmb
definitions.lean: def coeffEmb (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra ℚ L] : LaurentSeries ℚ →+* LaurentSeries L
definitions.math: The coefficient extension ℚ → K applied termwise to a Laurent series: the stand-in for 'base change to a field containing the roots of unity'.
definitions.heading: `coeffEmb` — coefficient extension

definitions.name: ModularCurve.jq
definitions.lean: def jq : LaurentSeries ℚ := HahnSeries.single (-1 : ℤ) 1 * HahnSeries.ofPowerSeries ℤ ℚ jNumQ
definitions.math: j(q) = q⁻¹ · (1 + 744 q + 196884 q² + ⋯), the j-invariant as a Laurent series over ℚ. It has a simple pole at q = 0 with residue 1; that single fact is the source of transcendence and of the triangularity arguments used in the segment.
definitions.heading: `jq` — the j-invariant as a Laurent series

definitions.name: ModularCurve.jqN
definitions.lean: def jqN (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] : LaurentSeries ℚ := qExpand ℚ N jq
definitions.math: j(q^N) := qExpand ℚ N j(q): the nome substitution q ↦ q^N applied to j(q).
definitions.heading: `jqN` — the substitution j(q^N)

definitions.name: ModularCurve.evalAtJ
definitions.lean: def evalAtJ : Polynomial ℤ →+* LaurentSeries ℚ := (Polynomial.aeval (R := ℤ) jq).toRingHom
definitions.math: Evaluation of an integer polynomial at j(q): the ring hom ℤ[X] → ℚ((q)), X ↦ j(q). For a two-variable modular polynomial Φ ∈ ℤ[X][Y], the outer evaluation is done with this map as the coefficient map and Y ↦ j(q^N): that is Φ.eval₂ evalAtJ (jqN N).
definitions.heading: `evalAtJ` — integer polynomial evaluation at j(q)

definitions.name: ModularCurve.evalAtJGen
definitions.lean: def evalAtJGen : Polynomial ℤ →+* ℚ⟮jq⟯ := Polynomial.eval₂RingHom (Int.castRingHom ℚ⟮jq⟯) jGen
definitions.math: The same evaluation X ↦ j(q), but valued in ℚ(j) rather than in ℚ((q)). It presents ℤ[j(q)] as a subring of ℚ(j(q)); it is injective because j(q) is transcendental, and ℚ(j(q)) is its fraction field.
definitions.heading: `evalAtJGen` — evaluation into ℚ(j)

definitions.name: ModularCurve.modularFunctionField
definitions.lean: def modularFunctionField (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] : IntermediateField ℚ (LaurentSeries ℚ) := IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ {jq, qExpand ℚ N jq}
definitions.math: F_N := ℚ(j(q), j(q^N)), the two-generator field of the theorem.
definitions.heading: `modularFunctionField` — the two-generator field F_N

definitions.name: ModularCurve.modularFunctionFieldFull
definitions.lean:
def modularFunctionFieldFull (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] : IntermediateField ℚ (LaurentSeries ℚ) :=
  IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (divisorExpansions N)
definitions.math: F_N^full := ℚ(j(q^d) : d ∣ N), the field generated by the divisor substitutions. The inclusion F_N ⊆ F_N^full is immediate (d = 1 and d = N); the theorem is the reverse inclusion.
definitions.heading: `modularFunctionFieldFull` — the divisor field F_N^full

definitions.name: ModularCurve.dedekindPsi
definitions.math: ψ(N) = Σ_{d ∣ N, d squarefree} N/d = N ∏_{p ∣ N}(1 + 1/p), the Dedekind psi function: the index of Γ₀(N) in SL₂(ℤ), the degree of X₀(N) → X(1), and the Y-degree of the modular equation Φ_N.
definitions.heading: `dedekindPsi` — the Dedekind psi function

definitions.name: ModularCurve.ModularPolynomialData
definitions.lean:
structure ModularPolynomialData (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] where
  Φ : Polynomial (Polynomial ℤ)
  monic : Φ.Monic
  natDegree_eq : Φ.natDegree = dedekindPsi N
  eval_eq_zero : Φ.eval₂ evalAtJ (jqN N) = 0
definitions.math: A modular polynomial datum at level N: Φ ∈ ℤ[X][Y] (outer variable Y, coefficients in ℤ[X] = ℤ[j]), monic in Y, of Y-degree ψ(N), and vanishing at X = j(q), Y = j(q^N).
definitions.heading: `ModularPolynomialData` — the modular polynomial datum

definitions.name: ModularCurve.ModularPolynomialData.toAdjoin
definitions.lean:
def ModularPolynomialData.toAdjoin {N : ℕ} [NeZero N] (data : ModularPolynomialData N) :
    Polynomial ℚ⟮jq⟯ := data.Φ.map evalAtJGen
definitions.math: The transport of Φ into ℚ(j)[Y]: evaluate every integer coefficient polynomial in ℤ[X] at j(q). This is the polynomial whose irreducibility over ℚ(j) is the content of PhiIrreducible.
definitions.heading: `toAdjoin` — transporting Φ into ℚ(j)[Y]

definitions.name: ModularCurve.PhiIrreducible
definitions.lean: def PhiIrreducible (data : ModularPolynomialData N) : Prop := Irreducible data.toAdjoin
definitions.math: The transported modular polynomial is irreducible over ℚ(j).
definitions.heading: `PhiIrreducible` — irreducibility over ℚ(j)

definitions.name: ModularCurve.FunctionFieldGeneration
definitions.math: FunctionFieldGeneration N: for every divisor d ∣ N, the series j(q^d) lies in the field ℚ(j(q), j(q^N)). This is the pointwise form of F_N^full = F_N.
definitions.heading: `FunctionFieldGeneration` — the pointwise target

definitions.name: ModularCurve.Tight
definitions.lean:
abbrev Tight (d : ℕ) [NeZero d] : Prop :=
  Module.finrank ℚ⟮jq⟯ (IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ⟮jq⟯ ({jqN d} : Set (LaurentSeries ℚ))) = dedekindPsi d
definitions.math: Tight d: the relative degree [ℚ(j)(j(q^d)) : ℚ(j)] equals ψ(d).
definitions.heading: `Tight` — the degree invariant

definitions.name: ModularCurve.Gen
definitions.lean: abbrev Gen (d : ℕ) [NeZero d] : Prop := modularFunctionField d = modularFunctionFieldFull d
definitions.math: Gen d: the two-generator field is already the full divisor field, F_d = F_d^full.
definitions.heading: `Gen` — the generation invariant

definitions.name: ModularCurve.Hall
definitions.lean: abbrev Hall (N : ℕ) : Prop := ∀ d : ℕ, d ∣ N → ∀ [NeZero d], Tight d ∧ Gen d
definitions.math: Hall N: the strong-induction hypothesis at N — both invariants hold at every divisor of N.
definitions.heading: `Hall` — the strong-induction bundle

definitions.name: ModularCurve.Inputs
definitions.lean:
structure Inputs where
  full_eq_adjoin_full_div_prime : …
  jqN_prime_not_mem_full : …
  jqN_pow_not_mem_adjoin_full : …
  minpoly_jqN_map_eq_prod_slots : …
  modularFunctionField_eq_full_of : …
  jqN_div_mem_modularFunctionField : …
  relfinrank_full_eq_mul : …
definitions.math: The seven significant statements of the segment, bundled as the hypotheses of the strong induction: two generation statements, two non-membership statements, the slot product, the one-prime reduction of Gen, and the prime-power degree step.
definitions.heading: `Inputs` — the seven significant statements
definitions.note: The seven field types are exhibited one by one, through the theorems that discharge them, in the reference zone; this entry only fixes the name and the shape of the bundle.

definitions.name: ModularCurve.phiAtSeed
definitions.lean:
def phiAtSeed {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]
    (data : ModularPolynomialData n) (x : R) : Polynomial R :=
  data.Φ.map (Polynomial.eval₂RingHom (Int.castRingHom R) x)
definitions.math: Φ(x, Y): the modular polynomial with its X-variable evaluated at x. At x = j(q^a) this is the monic polynomial in Y whose root is j(q^{an}).
definitions.heading: `phiAtSeed` — Φ evaluated at X = x

premises.label: hall_all
premises.name: ModularCurve.hall_all
premises.lean: theorem hall_all (h : Inputs) : ∀ N : ℕ, N ≠ 0 → Hall N
premises.math: From the seven inputs, Tight and Gen hold at every divisor of every N ≠ 0. This is the strong induction over the divisor lattice: the generation half walks down the divisors one prime at a time, and the degree half multiplies the tower law along prime-power levels.
premises.note: Its hypothesis is exactly `Inputs`; the proof is math/010 §7. The two halves are interdependent: Gen d needs Gen and the degree facts at proper divisors, Tight d needs Tight below and Gen d just proved.

premises.label: functionFieldGeneration_of
premises.name: ModularCurve.functionFieldGeneration_of
premises.lean: theorem functionFieldGeneration_of (h : Inputs) (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] : FunctionFieldGeneration N
premises.math: From the seven inputs, FunctionFieldGeneration N for every N ≠ 0. It is the packaged composition of `hall_all` at d = N with the collapse equivalence.

premises.label: iff_full_eq
premises.name: ModularCurve.functionFieldGeneration_iff_full_eq
premises.lean:
theorem functionFieldGeneration_iff_full_eq (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] :
    FunctionFieldGeneration N ↔ modularFunctionFieldFull N = modularFunctionField N
premises.math: The pointwise generation statement is equivalent to the field equality F_N^full = F_N. The forward direction says the field generated by all j(q^d) is contained in ℚ(j(q), j(q^N)); the reverse says every j(q^d) is among its generators.
premises.note: The right-hand side is written with F_N^full on the left. `Gen N` is the opposite orientation, F_N = F_N^full, so a proof must use `.symm` — this is the one place where the capstone's one-liners are orientation-sensitive.

premises.label: relfinrank_modularFunctionField
premises.name: ModularCurve.relfinrank_modularFunctionField
premises.lean:
theorem relfinrank_modularFunctionField (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] :
    IntermediateField.relfinrank ℚ⟮jq⟯ (modularFunctionField N) =
    Module.finrank ℚ⟮jq⟯ (IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ⟮jq⟯ ({jqN N} : Set (LaurentSeries ℚ)))
premises.math: The relative degree [F_N : ℚ(j)] is the degree of the simple extension ℚ(j)(j(q^N)). Equivalently: adjoining the single element j(q^N) to ℚ(j) gives F_N, so the relative degree is the degree of j(q^N) over ℚ(j).

premises.label: full_eq_adjoin_full_div_prime
premises.name: ModularCurve.full_eq_adjoin_full_div_prime
premises.lean:
theorem full_eq_adjoin_full_div_prime (M : ℕ) [NeZero M] (p : ℕ)
    [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (a : ℕ) (hpM : ¬ p ∣ M) :
    modularFunctionFieldFull (M * p ^ (a + 1)) =
      IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ
        (insert (jqN (p ^ (a + 1))) (modularFunctionFieldFull (M * p ^ a) : Set (LaurentSeries ℚ)))
premises.math: For p ∤ M, the full field at M p^{a+1} is generated over the full field at M p^a by the single new series j(q^{p^{a+1}}). This is the generation half of one prime-power step (T18).
premises.note: Proof: the inclusion ⊇ is immediate because both generators divide M p^{a+1}. For ⊆, take j(q^d) with d ∣ M p^{a+1}. If d ∣ M p^a it is already in the lower field; otherwise d = m p^{a+1} with m ∣ M, p ∤ m. If m = 1 it is the new generator; if m > 1 pick a prime q ∣ m, q ≠ p, and apply the two-prime descent: j(q^{d/p}) is in the target by inspection and j(q^{d/q}) by strong induction, and the unique common root of Φ_p and Φ_q forces j(q^d) in the target.

premises.label: jqN_prime_not_mem_full
premises.name: ModularCurve.jqN_prime_not_mem_full
premises.lean:
theorem jqN_prime_not_mem_full (M : ℕ) [NeZero M] (p : ℕ)
    [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (hpM : ¬ p ∣ M) (hall : Hall M) :
    jqN p ∉ modularFunctionFieldFull M
premises.math: For p ∤ M and Hall M, j(q^p) is not in the full field at M. This is one of the two non-membership inputs of the degree half (T19).
premises.note: Proof: if j(q^p) were in F_M^full, then by Gen M it would lie in ℚ(j)(j(q^M)), say j(q^p) = g(j(q^M)) with deg g < ψ(M). Evaluating g at the ψ(M) distinct slots of the minimal polynomial of j(q^M) shows g is constant there; a polynomial of degree < ψ(M) constant on ψ(M) points has its value in ℚ(j). Then j(q^p) ∈ ℚ(j), contradicting the prime-level degree [ℚ(j)(j(q^p)) : ℚ(j)] = p + 1. The theorem states the hypothesis as the expanded conjunction ∀ d ∣ M, Tight d ∧ Gen d; that is definitionally `Hall M`, because Hall is an abbreviation, which is why `inputs` can fill the field with it.

premises.label: jqN_pow_not_mem_adjoin_full
premises.name: ModularCurve.jqN_pow_not_mem_adjoin_full
premises.lean:
theorem jqN_pow_not_mem_adjoin_full (M : ℕ) [NeZero M] (p : ℕ)
    [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (a : ℕ)
    (hF : jqN p ∉ modularFunctionFieldFull M) :
    jqN (p ^ (a + 2)) ∉ IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ
      ((modularFunctionFieldFull M : Set (LaurentSeries ℚ))
        ∪ {x : LaurentSeries ℚ | ∃ i : ℕ, i ≤ a + 1 ∧ x = jqN (p ^ i)})
premises.math: If j(q^p) is not in F_M^full, then j(q^{p^{a+2}}) is not in the field generated by F_M^full together with the earlier p-power series j(q^p), …, j(q^{p^{a+1}}). This is the prime-power non-membership tower (T17).
premises.note: Proof: build the tower of intermediate fields and a compatible family of ℚ-algebra homs σ_i whose images lie in a shrinking qExpand range. The modular equation Φ_p has both j(q^{p^{a+2}}) and j(q^{p^a}) as roots of Φ_p(j(q^{p^{a+1}}), Y); pushing it through σ forces the two to be the same root, and injectivity of σ gives equality of the two series, contradicted by the q^{-(p^a)} coefficient (1 versus 0).

premises.label: minpoly_jqN_map_eq_prod_slots
premises.name: ModularCurve.minpoly_jqN_map_eq_prod_slots
premises.lean:
theorem minpoly_jqN_map_eq_prod_slots {K : Type*} [Field K] [Algebra ℚ K]
    (M : ℕ) [NeZero M] (ζ : Kˣ) (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot (ζ : K) M) (hall : Hall M) :
    (minpoly ℚ⟮jq⟯ (jqN M)).map (((coeffEmb K).comp (qExpand ℚ M)).comp
      (algebraMap ℚ⟮jq⟯ (LaurentSeries ℚ)))
    = ∏ a ∈ M.divisors, ∏ b ∈ (Finset.range (M / a)).filter
        (fun b => Nat.gcd (Nat.gcd a b) (M / a) = 1),
      (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C (if h : a = 0 then 0 else
        qExpand K (a * a) (qTwist (ζ ^ (b * a)) (coeffEmb K jq))))
premises.math: The slot description of the conjugates: after the coefficient substitution q ↦ q^M, the minimal polynomial of j(q^M) over ℚ(j) is the product of the linear factors Y − j(ζ^{ab} q^{a²}), over a ∣ M and 0 ≤ b < M/a with gcd(gcd(a,b), M/a) = 1. The pairs number ψ(M).
premises.note: Proof (T19): iterate the prime-level splitting Φ_p(j(u^p q^{pe}), Y) = (Y − j(u^{p²}q^{p²e})) ∏_b (Y − j(u ζ_p^b q^e)) over the prime factorization of M. The exponent a² and the root of unity ζ^{ab} are the coset data.

premises.label: modularFunctionField_eq_full_of
premises.name: ModularCurve.modularFunctionField_eq_full_of
premises.lean:
theorem modularFunctionField_eq_full_of (N : ℕ) [NeZero N]
    (hstep : ∀ (M : ℕ) [NeZero M] (p : ℕ), p.Prime → M * p = N →
      jqN M ∈ modularFunctionField N)
    (hgen : ∀ (M : ℕ) [NeZero M] (p : ℕ), p.Prime → M * p = N →
      modularFunctionField M = modularFunctionFieldFull M) :
    modularFunctionField N = modularFunctionFieldFull N
premises.math: The one-prime reduction of Gen N: if every factorization N = M·p with p prime has j(q^M) ∈ F_N and Gen M, then F_N = F_N^full.
premises.note: Proof: the reverse inclusion is modularFunctionField_le_full. For the forward one, take j(q^d) with d ∣ N, d ≠ N, write N = d·m, pick a prime p ∣ m and m = p·m′. Then N = (d m′)·p, so j(q^{d m′}) ∈ F_N by hstep and Gen(d m′) is hgen; hence j(q^d) ∈ F_{d m′} ⊆ F_N.

premises.label: jqN_div_mem_modularFunctionField
premises.name: ModularCurve.jqN_div_mem_modularFunctionField
premises.lean:
theorem jqN_div_mem_modularFunctionField (M : ℕ) [NeZero M] (p : ℕ)
    [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] {K : Type*} [Field K] [Algebra ℚ K] (ζ : Kˣ)
    (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot (ζ : K) (M * p))
    (htw : ∀ y, Polynomial.eval y (minpoly ℚ⟮jq⟯ (jqN M)).map ⋯ = 0 →
      ∀ w : Kˣ, y = qExpand K (M * p * M) (qTwist w (coeffEmb K jq)) → w = 1)
    (hsp : ∀ y, Polynomial.eval y (minpoly ℚ⟮jq⟯ (jqN M)).map ⋯ = 0 →
      y ≠ coeffEmb K (qExpand ℚ (M * p) (jqN (M * p * p)))) :
    jqN M ∈ modularFunctionField (M * p)
premises.math: Descent by one prime: under the two slot hypotheses htw and hsp, j(q^M) lies in ℚ(j(q), j(q^{Mp})). The hypotheses say: a common root of the pushed minimal polynomial that has the shape j(w q^{M²p}) has w = 1 (htw), and the extra root j(q^{M²p³}) is not a common root (hsp).
premises.note: Proof (T15): the unique-common-root principle. Take A = Φ_p(j(q^{Mp}), Y) and B = the push of minpoly_ℚ(j)(j(q^M)) into F = ℚ(j(q), j(q^{Mp})); x₀ = j(q^M) is a common root by the modular equation and by symmetry. The slot description lists all roots, and htw/hsp leave x₀ as the only common one. Hence x₀ ∈ F. The tail strips the coefficient extension by injectivity of coeffEmb and qExpand. The `lean` field abbreviates the two slot hypotheses with ⋯; the sheet's `#check` is the full type.

premises.label: relfinrank_full_eq_mul
premises.name: ModularCurve.relfinrank_full_eq_mul
premises.lean:
theorem relfinrank_full_eq_mul (M : ℕ) [NeZero M] (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (a : ℕ)
    (hup : modularFunctionFieldFull (M * p ^ (a + 1)) =
      IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (insert (jqN (p ^ (a + 1)))
        (modularFunctionFieldFull (M * p ^ a) : Set (LaurentSeries ℚ))))
    (hnm : jqN (p ^ (a + 1)) ∉ modularFunctionFieldFull (M * p ^ a)) :
    IntermediateField.relfinrank (modularFunctionFieldFull (M * p ^ a))
      (modularFunctionFieldFull (M * p ^ (a + 1))) = if a = 0 then p + 1 else p
premises.math: The relative degree of one full prime-power step is p + 1 for the first step (a = 0) and p for later steps. This is the degree half of the induction (T16).
premises.note: Proof: by the tower equality the step is a simple extension, so w1_relfinrank_insert reduces to the degree of j(q^{p^{a+1}}) over the lower field. For a = 0 that degree is p + 1 (the degree of Φ_p; irreducibility from a transitive automorphism cycling the p + 1 roots). For a ≥ 1, Φ_p(j(q^{p^{a+1}}), Y) already has the root j(q^{p^a}) in the lower field, so it factors as (Y − j(q^{p^a}))·P with deg P = p, and P is irreducible by a coefficient automorphism argument.

premises.label: exists_phiIrreducible_evalSymm
premises.name: ModularCurve.exists_phiIrreducible_evalSymm
premises.lean:
theorem exists_phiIrreducible_evalSymm (ℓ : ℕ) [hℓ : Fact (Nat.Prime ℓ)] :
    ∃ data : ModularPolynomialData ℓ, PhiIrreducible data ∧ EvalSymm data.Φ
premises.math: At every prime ℓ there is a modular polynomial datum at level ℓ whose Φ is symmetric in its two variables (and irreducible). Only monicity and the vanishing at (j(q), j(q^ℓ)) are used by the integrality proof; symmetry is used by the descent and the slot product.
premises.note: This is the classical prime-level splitting input, read as an existence statement: Φ_ℓ(j(u^ℓ q^{ℓe}), Y) = (Y − j(u^{ℓ²}q^{ℓ²e})) ∏_{b<ℓ}(Y − j(u ζ_ℓ^b q^e)). The proof is in ModularPolynomialProperties.lean (T12).

premises.label: evalAtJGen_injective
premises.name: ModularCurve.evalAtJGen_injective
premises.lean: theorem evalAtJGen_injective : Function.Injective (evalAtJGen : Polynomial ℤ →+* ↥ℚ⟮jq⟯)
premises.math: Evaluation ℤ[X] → ℚ(j), X ↦ j(q), is injective: j(q) is transcendental over ℚ. This is what lets ℤ[j] be identified with a subring of ℚ(j).
premises.note: The port proves it from the q^{-natDegree} coefficient of p(j(q)) being the leading coefficient of p — the simple-pole triangularity — and uses it to transport injectivity from the Laurent series into ℚ(j).

premises.label: algebraMap_comp_evalAtJGen
premises.name: ModularCurve.algebraMap_comp_evalAtJGen
premises.lean:
theorem algebraMap_comp_evalAtJGen :
    (algebraMap ℚ⟮jq⟯ (LaurentSeries ℚ)).comp evalAtJGen = evalAtJ
premises.math: The inclusion ℚ(j) ↪ ℚ((q)) composed with the evaluation ℤ[X] → ℚ(j) is exactly the evaluation ℤ[X] → ℚ((q)): evaluating at j(q) and then viewing the result as a series is evaluating at j(q) directly.

premises.label: jqN_one
premises.name: ModularCurve.jqN_one
premises.lean: theorem jqN_one : jqN 1 = jq

premises.label: jqN_congr
premises.name: ModularCurve.jqN_congr
premises.lean: theorem jqN_congr {n m : ℕ} [NeZero n] [NeZero m] (h : n = m) : jqN n = jqN m
premises.math: j(q^n) depends only on the level n: equal exponents give equal series.

premises.label: evalAtJ_X
premises.name: ModularCurve.evalAtJ_X
premises.lean: theorem evalAtJ_X : evalAtJ Polynomial.X = jq
premises.math: The polynomial X evaluates to j(q): X is a monic annihilator of j(q).

premises.label: transcendental_jq
premises.name: ModularCurve.transcendental_jq
premises.lean: theorem transcendental_jq : Transcendental ℚ jq
premises.math: j(q) is transcendental over ℚ. The reason is the simple pole at q = 0: a nonzero polynomial relation would have a leading coefficient that fails to vanish at the pole.

premises.label: dedekindPsi_prime
premises.name: ModularCurve.dedekindPsi_prime
premises.lean: theorem dedekindPsi_prime {p : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) : dedekindPsi p = p + 1
premises.math: ψ(p) = p + 1: the modular equation at a prime has degree p + 1.

premises.label: phiAtSeed_monic
premises.name: ModularCurve.phiAtSeed_monic
premises.lean: theorem phiAtSeed_monic (data : ModularPolynomialData n) (x : R) : (phiAtSeed data x).Monic
premises.math: Φ(x, Y) is monic in Y, because Φ is monic in Y and evaluation of the X-variable preserves monicity.

premises.label: phiAtSeed_map
premises.name: ModularCurve.phiAtSeed_map
premises.lean:
theorem phiAtSeed_map (data : ModularPolynomialData n) (x : R) (f : R →+* S) :
    (phiAtSeed data x).map f = phiAtSeed data (f x)
premises.math: Φ(x, Y) is natural in the coefficient ring: pushing the polynomial along a ring map f is the same as evaluating X at f(x) in the target.

premises.label: phiAtSeed_jqN_eval
premises.name: ModularCurve.phiAtSeed_jqN_eval
premises.lean:
theorem phiAtSeed_jqN_eval (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (data : ModularPolynomialData n)
    (M : ℕ) [NeZero M] :
    (phiAtSeed data (jqN M)).eval (jqN (M * n)) = 0
premises.math: Φ(j(q^M), j(q^{Mn})) = 0: substituting q ↦ q^M into the modular equation Φ(j(q), j(q^n)) = 0 gives a vanishing at the corresponding pair of levels.

premises.label: induction_on_primes
premises.name: induction_on_primes
premises.lean:
induction_on_primes (zero : motive 0) (one : motive 1)
    (prime_mul : ∀ p a, p.Prime → motive a → motive (p * a)) : ∀ n, motive n
premises.math: Induction on the multiplicative structure of ℕ: the base cases 0 and 1, and a step that multiplies an arbitrary level by a prime.

premises.label: isIntegral_algebraMap
premises.name: isIntegral_algebraMap
premises.lean: theorem isIntegral_algebraMap {x : R} : IsIntegral R (algebraMap R A x)
premises.math: Every element of the image of the base ring is integral; X is its own monic annihilator.

premises.label: IsIntegral.fg_adjoin_singleton
premises.name: IsIntegral.fg_adjoin_singleton
premises.lean: theorem IsIntegral.fg_adjoin_singleton {x : B} : IsIntegral R x → (Subalgebra.toSubmodule R[x]).FG
premises.math: Adjoining a single integral element produces a finitely generated module: if x is integral over R, then R[x] is a finite R-module.

premises.label: IsIntegral.of_mem_of_fg
premises.name: IsIntegral.of_mem_of_fg
premises.lean: theorem IsIntegral.of_mem_of_fg (S : Subalgebra R B) (HS : S.toSubmodule.FG) (x : B) (hx : x ∈ S) : IsIntegral R x
premises.math: If a subalgebra S is finitely generated as an R-module, every element of S is integral over R.

premises.label: isIntegral_algHom_iff
premises.name: isIntegral_algHom_iff
premises.lean: theorem isIntegral_algHom_iff (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (hf : Function.Injective f) {x : A} : IsIntegral R (f x) ↔ IsIntegral R x
premises.math: An injective R-algebra map reflects integrality: x is integral over R exactly when its image is.

premises.label: isIntegral_trans
premises.name: isIntegral_trans
premises.lean: theorem isIntegral_trans [Algebra.IsIntegral R A] (x : B) (hx : IsIntegral A x) : IsIntegral R x
premises.math: Transitivity of integrality: if A is integral over R and x is integral over A, then x is integral over R.

premises.label: IsIntegral.tower_top
premises.name: IsIntegral.tower_top
premises.lean: theorem IsIntegral.tower_top [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower R A B] {x : B} : IsIntegral R x → IsIntegral A x
premises.math: Enlarging the base ring preserves integrality: integral over R implies integral over any R-algebra A in a scalar tower.

premises.label: minpoly.isIntegrallyClosed_eq_field_fractions'
premises.name: minpoly.isIntegrallyClosed_eq_field_fractions'
premises.lean:
theorem minpoly.isIntegrallyClosed_eq_field_fractions' (K : Type*) [Field K]
    [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K] [IsIntegrallyClosed R] [IsDomain S]
    [Algebra K S] [IsScalarTower R K S] {s : S} (hs : IsIntegral R s) :
    minpoly K s = (minpoly R s).map (algebraMap R K)
premises.math: Over an integrally closed base ring R with fraction field K, the minimal polynomial over K is the image of the minimal polynomial over R.

premises.label: minpoly.monic
premises.name: minpoly.monic
premises.lean: theorem minpoly.monic {x : B} : IsIntegral A x → (minpoly A x).Monic
premises.math: A minimal polynomial of an integral element is monic.

premises.label: minpoly.aeval
premises.name: minpoly.aeval
premises.lean: theorem minpoly.aeval (x : B) : aeval x (minpoly A x) = 0
premises.math: The defining property of the minimal polynomial: it annihilates its element.

premises.label: minpoly.irreducible
premises.name: minpoly.irreducible
premises.lean: theorem minpoly.irreducible [IsDomain A] [IsDomain B] : IsIntegral A x → Irreducible (minpoly A x)
premises.math: The minimal polynomial of an element over a field is irreducible.

premises.label: IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank
premises.name: IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank
premises.lean: theorem IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank {x : L} (hx : IsIntegral K x) : Module.finrank K K⟮x⟯ = (minpoly K x).natDegree
premises.math: The degree of a simple extension equals the degree of the minimal polynomial: [K(x) : K] = deg(minpoly_K x).

premises.label: IsLocalization.integerNormalization_spec
premises.name: IsLocalization.integerNormalization_spec
premises.lean:
theorem IsLocalization.integerNormalization_spec (M : Submonoid R) (p : S[X]) :
    ∃ b ∈ M, Polynomial.map (algebraMap R S)
      (IsLocalization.integerNormalization M p) = b • p
premises.math: Denominator clearing: for a localized ring S and a polynomial p over S, some integer multiple of p (by an element b of the localization submonoid) comes from a polynomial over R, namely integerNormalization p.

premises.label: IntermediateField.mem_adjoin_simple_iff
premises.name: IntermediateField.mem_adjoin_simple_iff
premises.lean: theorem IntermediateField.mem_adjoin_simple_iff {α : E} (x : E) : x ∈ F⟮α⟯ ↔ ∃ r s, x = aeval α r / aeval α s
premises.math: Every element of a simple extension F(α) is a quotient of two polynomial expressions in α over F.

premises.label: Polynomial.eval₂_eq_eval_map
premises.name: Polynomial.eval₂_eq_eval_map
premises.lean: theorem Polynomial.eval₂_eq_eval_map (f : R →+* S) {x : S} : p.eval₂ f x = (p.map f).eval x
premises.math: Evaluating with a coefficient map f at x is evaluating the mapped polynomial at x.

premises.label: Polynomial.aeval_def
premises.name: Polynomial.aeval_def
premises.lean: theorem Polynomial.aeval_def (x : A) (p : R[X]) : aeval x p = eval₂ (algebraMap R A) x p
premises.math: Algebra evaluation is evaluation with the algebra map as coefficient map.

premises.label: Polynomial.Monic.natDegree_map
premises.name: Polynomial.Monic.natDegree_map
premises.lean: theorem Polynomial.Monic.natDegree_map {P : R[X]} (hP : P.Monic) (f : R →+* S) : (P.map f).natDegree = P.natDegree
premises.math: Mapping a monic polynomial along a ring hom preserves its degree.

declarations.name: ModularCurve.inputs
declarations.heading: `inputs` — the seven significant statements, discharged
declarations.lean:
theorem inputs : Inputs where
  full_eq_adjoin_full_div_prime := full_eq_adjoin_full_div_prime
  jqN_prime_not_mem_full := jqN_prime_not_mem_full
  jqN_pow_not_mem_adjoin_full := jqN_pow_not_mem_adjoin_full
  minpoly_jqN_map_eq_prod_slots := minpoly_jqN_map_eq_prod_slots
  modularFunctionField_eq_full_of := modularFunctionField_eq_full_of
  jqN_div_mem_modularFunctionField := jqN_div_mem_modularFunctionField
  relfinrank_full_eq_mul := relfinrank_full_eq_mul
declarations.math_statement: The conjunction of the seven statements bundled in `Inputs` holds. Concretely: (1) one new generator per prime power, F_{Mp^{a+1}}^full = ℚ(F_{Mp^a}^full, j(q^{p^{a+1}})) for p ∤ M; (2) j(q^p) ∉ F_M^full for p ∤ M and Hall M; (3) j(q^{p^{a+2}}) ∉ ℚ(F_M^full, j(q^p), …, j(q^{p^{a+1}})) given j(q^p) ∉ F_M^full; (4) the slot product for the conjugates of j(q^M); (5) the one-prime reduction of Gen; (6) descent by one prime, given the two slot hypotheses; (7) the prime-power degree step.
declarations.role: Turns the conditional capstone into an unconditional one. After T15–T19 there is no assumed statement left in the segment.

proof.goal: Produce a term of type `Inputs`: a proof of each of its seven fields.
proof.strategy: There is no mathematical work left. Each field is the conclusion of a theorem already proved, stated with the same binders and hypotheses so that discharging the field is a drop-in replacement. The Lean term is the structure literal that names the seven theorems.

steps.math: For M ≠ 0, p prime, p ∤ M and a ≥ 0: F_{M p^{a+1}}^full = ℚ(F_{M p^a}^full, j(q^{p^{a+1}})).
steps.why: This is T18. The two-prime descent walks d ∣ M p^{a+1}: if d ∣ M p^a the series is already in the lower field; otherwise peel a prime q ≠ p from the M-part, and the unique common root of Φ_p and Φ_q puts j(q^d) in the target. The field type is the theorem's conclusion verbatim, with the same binders and hypotheses, so no premise needs adaptation; the same holds for the remaining six fields.

steps.math: For p ∤ M and Hall M: j(q^p) ∉ F_M^full.
steps.why: This is T19. If j(q^p) were in F_M^full, Gen M would put it in ℚ(j)(j(q^M)); evaluating at the ψ(M) distinct slots of the minimal polynomial of j(q^M) would force j(q^p) ∈ ℚ(j), contradicting the prime-level degree p + 1.

steps.math: Given j(q^p) ∉ F_M^full: j(q^{p^{a+2}}) ∉ ℚ(F_M^full ∪ {j(q^{p^i}) : 0 ≤ i ≤ a + 1}).
steps.why: This is T17. The tower of compatible algebra homs and the modular equation Φ_p force j(q^{p^{a+2}}) and j(q^{p^a}) to be the same root; injectivity gives equality of the series, contradicted by the q^{-(p^a)} coefficient.

steps.math: For a field K with a ℚ-algebra structure, a primitive M-th root of unity ζ, and Hall M: the transported minimal polynomial of j(q^M) is the ψ(M)-fold product over the slots (a, b), a ∣ M, 0 ≤ b < M/a, gcd(gcd(a,b), M/a) = 1, of Y − j(ζ^{ab} q^{a²}).
steps.why: This is T19. Iterate the prime-level splitting of Φ_p over the prime factorization of M; the exponent a² and the root of unity ζ^{ab} are the coset data.

steps.math: If for every factorization N = M·p with p prime one has j(q^M) ∈ F_N and Gen M, then F_N = F_N^full.
steps.why: This is T15. Take d ∣ N, d ≠ N, write N = d·m, pick a prime p ∣ m and m = p·m′. Then j(q^{d m′}) ∈ F_N and Gen(d m′) give j(q^d) ∈ F_N.

steps.math: For p prime, a primitive (Mp)-th root of unity ζ, and the slot hypotheses htw and hsp: j(q^M) ∈ ℚ(j(q), j(q^{Mp})).
steps.why: This is T15. The unique-common-root principle applied to A = Φ_p(j(q^{Mp}), Y) and the pushed minimal polynomial of j(q^M); htw and hsp leave j(q^M) as the only common root.

steps.math: Given the tower equality F_{M p^{a+1}}^full = ℚ(F_{M p^a}^full, j(q^{p^{a+1}})) and the non-membership j(q^{p^{a+1}}) ∉ F_{M p^a}^full: [F_{M p^{a+1}}^full : F_{M p^a}^full] = p + 1 if a = 0, else p.
steps.why: This is T16. The simple-extension reduction, then the degree p + 1 of the first prime power and the degree p of later ones; ψ(p) = p + 1 is the Dedekind value the induction compares against.

steps.claim: The structure literal with these seven proofs is a term of type `Inputs`.
steps.why: Lean elaborates each field against its stated type; the seven steps fill exactly those types.

regeneration: Fill each structure field with the theorem of the same name; do not restate or adapt any type.
If a field fails to elaborate, the port's statement has drifted from the theorem's — that is a real bug, not a proof obligation.
The same seven theorems can be passed to `hall_all` directly (FLT's route); the bundle exists so that discharging a field is a one-line change.
formal_notes: `Inputs` has only proposition-valued fields, so Lean places it in `Prop`; a term of it is a proof of the conjunction.
Inside the structure literal, the right-hand side of each `field := ...` resolves to the namespace-level theorem of the same name (the field name is not a local variable).
The assembly has no pin counterpart: FLT's `hall_all` consumes the seven statements directly, without bundling.

provenance.flt: Port assembly only: FLT has no bundled counterpart (hall_all consumes the seven statements directly).

sections.title: the statement, in mathematical form
sections.prose:
The theorem is classical: over ℚ, the function field of X₀(N) is generated by the two functions j(q) and j(q^N). The formalization has no Riemann surface; it builds X₀(N) from the divisor field F_N^full, so the theorem is the collapse F_N^full = F_N.

Two numbers govern the proof. ψ(N) is the degree of the cover X₀(N) → X(1) and the Y-degree of the modular equation Φ_N. The other is the relative degree [ℚ(j)(j(q^N)) : ℚ(j)], which the theorem proves equals ψ(N). Generation and degree are proved together, by one strong induction over the divisor lattice; this presentation starts from the end of that induction (the assembly in Capstone.lean) and then reads the two input-supplying theorems that are proved inside the file.

Everything lives in the single field ℚ((q)) of Laurent series. The substitutions are ring endomorphisms — q ↦ q^N and q ↦ u q^e — not analytic maps, and no analytic continuation is used anywhere.

sections.title: the strong induction and its seven inputs
sections.tagline: Tight, Gen, Hall, and the bundle of significant statements
sections.prose:
The induction carries two invariants at every divisor: Tight (the degree of the modular equation at that level is full) and Gen (the two-generator field is already the whole divisor field). Together they form Hall. The engine is `hall_all`, whose hypotheses are the seven significant statements bundled in `Inputs`.

T15–T19 proved all seven. `inputs` is therefore the point where the segment stops assuming anything: it is not a mathematical theorem but the seven proofs assembled. The presentation below records, for each field, what the field says mathematically and which theorem discharges it. The proofs of the seven theorems are elsewhere; what matters here is that their statements are the field statements verbatim, so each discharge is a drop-in replacement rather than an adaptation.

sections.title: the capstone and its corollary layer
sections.prose: With `inputs` in hand the main theorem is a one-liner, and so are the three corollaries the rest of FLT consumes: the field equality, the degree of the modular equation, and the relative degree of the full field. The mathematics is entirely in `hall_all` and in the seven field theorems. What this section presents is the assembly, the orientation of the equalities, and the two bridges that turn `Tight` into a statement about F_N^full.

sections.title: integrality — the monic annihilator
sections.tagline: the modular equation as a monic polynomial over ℤ[j]
sections.prose:
Integrality of j(q^N) over ℤ[j(q)] is the existence of the modular equation as a monic polynomial. The proof is an induction on the multiplicative structure of N: at each prime p, the modular polynomial Φ_p supplies a monic annihilator of j(q^{ap}) over ℤ[j][j(q^a)], and integrality is transitive. The only external input is the prime-level existence of Φ_p.

The three private lemmas at the top of this section are formal bridges, not mathematics: they move a value between ℚ(j) and ℚ((q)), and between integer and rational coefficients. They are stated here because the fraction-field argument in the next section uses them.

sections.title: from the degree count to an irreducible datum
sections.tagline: two minimal polynomials and a fraction field
sections.prose:
The last step turns the degree count into an irreducible modular polynomial. The key is to compare two minimal polynomials: over ℤ[j(q)] (where j(q^N) is integral) and over ℚ(j(q)) (its fraction field). The fraction-field structure is the only technical point; after it, the degree computation and irreducibility are consequences of the minimal-polynomial API.

The three exports differ only in packaging: the construction with its hypothesis, the hypothesis-free existence of an irreducible datum, and the bare existence of a datum. The last one is a deliberate strengthening over the pin's separate proof.

The port group contains the seven `Inputs` fields together with the induction engine and the bridges; the mathlib group contains the generic lemmas the two proof-bearing declarations invoke. `#check` shows the type as the compiler sees it; the gloss under each name says what it means mathematically.

sections.title: formalization notes — the Lean detours
sections.tagline: what is plumbing and what is mathematics
sections.prose:
Four formal devices recur; none carries mathematical content.

**Instances and positivity.** Every level is a natural number with a `NeZero` instance. The substitution q ↦ q^0 is the zero map, and j(q^0) is not a q-expansion, so the level must be positive. The `NeZero` arguments are discharged by `NeZero.ne` or built from `NeZero (p·a)`; they are not hypotheses of the mathematics.

**`eval₂` versus `aeval`.** The port evaluates integer polynomials with `evalAtJ`, a ring hom ℤ[X] → ℚ((q)). Mathlib's `aeval` uses the algebra structure instead. The bridges `aeval_map_intCast` and `algebraMap_comp_evalAtJGen` make the two agree, and the two `letI := ....toAlgebra` lines in the fraction-field proof install the algebra structures that `minpoly` and `IsIntegral` expect.

**Private helpers.** `coe_evalAtJGen`, `aeval_map_intCast` and `evalAtJ_C` are `private` to Capstone.lean and cannot be `#check`ed from another module. This sheet exhibits their statements as closed Lean propositions (`#check (… : Prop)`), which typecheck against the public API without naming the private declarations.

**Orientation.** The two function fields are equated in both orientations in the sources. `Gen d` is F_d = F_d^full; the collapse equivalence is stated with F_N^full on the left. Rewriting the wrong way is the most common failure mode in this file, so each equality above records which orientation the proof uses.
